questions.question: What is the core release invariant for this system?
options: Every accepted job must finish in under 10 seconds.
Release only an image with authorized likeness, faithful identity, and passing professional and safety checks.
A headshot must maximize an aesthetic preference score before delivery.
Every uploaded photo must produce at least one final image.
questions.explanation: Fast completion and visual appeal matter, but neither authorizes likeness use nor proves that the output faithfully represents the consenting subject.

questions.question: The baseline calls for 50,000 final images per day and 2.5 preview candidates per final image. How many preview candidates should capacity planning include per day?
questions.explanation: Preview work is 50,000 final images multiplied by 2.5 candidates each, or 125,000 candidates per day.

questions.question: Why should the job controller own durable state rather than the accelerator worker?
options: It lets the model choose any style without a policy record.
It allows a worker to keep image bytes in a queue message.
It makes stage retries, leases, cancellation, and duplicate messages auditable and idempotent.
It removes the need to store model and policy versions.
questions.explanation: A durable job record gives the system a single source of truth for attempts and dispositions, so a replayed message cannot create two released outputs.

questions.question: A generated candidate has excellent composition but borderline identity similarity. What is the correct release behavior?
options: Release it because professional quality is high.
Lower the similarity threshold for this job only.
Route it to review or request better inputs; do not release it automatically.
Replace the uncertain face with a more polished synthetic face.
questions.explanation: Composition is independent evidence. Ambiguous identity evidence must not be converted into an automatic likeness release.

questions.question: Which enterprise brand control is safest to introduce first?
options: A tenant-scoped, reviewed preset with a versioned background class, crop range, lighting target, and allowed attire categories.
An unrestricted natural-language prompt that can reshape any subject to match the brand.
One shared fine-tuned model trained on all companies' employee photos.
A rule that changes facial features until every employee has the same look.
questions.explanation: Bounded, versioned presets preserve tenant isolation and make the visual policy reviewable and reversible.

questions.question: What should happen if the identity-verification dependency is unavailable after a final candidate has rendered?
options: Publish the candidate because rendering already completed.
Retry delivery until the user accepts a download without verification.
Keep the candidate quarantined and stop final release until verification recovers or the job reaches a defined safe resolution.
Skip identity checks only for enterprise batch jobs.
questions.explanation: The system may delay delivery or give an honest status, but it must not bypass the independent release gate for an unverified likeness.
